services.name: Air Conditioning
services.summary: Installation, repair, and tune-up for all AC systems
services.details: Whether your central AC unit has stopped working in a SoCal heat wave or you're building a new home and need a complete system installed, Steve's has the experience to handle it. We service all major brands including Carrier, Lennox, Trane, Rheem, Goodman, Daikin, and more. Our technicians diagnose problems fast and fix them right — without recommending unnecessary repairs. We also offer ductless mini-split installation for garages, additions, and spaces difficult to cool with central systems.

services.name: Furnaces
services.summary: Gas, electric, and propane furnace installation and repair
services.details: Southern California winters may be mild compared to the rest of the country, but temperatures in the Temecula Valley can drop sharply at night. Steve's installs and services natural gas, electric, and propane furnaces for homes of all sizes. If your furnace is short-cycling, producing strange noises, heating unevenly, or driving your gas bill sky-high, call us for a diagnostic.

services.name: Heat Pumps
services.details: Heat pumps are one of the most energy-efficient ways to heat and cool your home — ideal for the mild SoCal climate. A single system does the work of both a furnace and an AC unit, moving heat rather than generating it, which means dramatically lower energy bills year-round. We install and service air-source and ground-source heat pumps for residential and light commercial applications.

services.name: Residential Refrigeration
services.details: From custom wine cellars to residential walk-in coolers, Steve's handles the full range of residential refrigeration. Our technicians are certified in refrigerant handling and skilled in both installation and repair of specialty cold storage systems.

services.name: Commercial Refrigeration
services.details: Restaurant walk-ins, commercial freezers, refrigerated display cases — a refrigeration failure means lost product and lost revenue. Steve's provides rapid-response commercial refrigeration repair and full system installation for businesses throughout SW Riverside County. We work around your schedule to minimize downtime.

services.name: HVAC Maintenance
services.summary: Keep it running before it breaks
services.details: The single best way to avoid a mid-summer AC emergency is a proper spring tune-up. Our maintenance service includes a comprehensive system inspection, cleaning of all critical components, refrigerant level check, and a full performance test. We document everything and give you a plain-language report on your system's condition.

faqs.q: Can you install a brand I purchase myself?
faqs.a: Call us about that one — equipment-supplied installs are case-by-case. We need to make sure the equipment is right for your home and that any factory warranty isn't voided by the install.

faqs.q: How often should I have my HVAC serviced?
faqs.a: Once a year minimum — ideally a spring AC tune-up and a fall furnace inspection. Annual maintenance catches small problems before they become emergency failures and keeps your system running efficiently.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a heat pump and a regular AC?
faqs.a: A heat pump moves heat in either direction, so it can both cool your home in summer AND heat it in winter — a single system replacing both your AC and furnace. They're very efficient in mild climates like ours, which means lower energy bills year-round. A regular AC only cools.

faqs.q: How long does a new HVAC system last?
faqs.a: With proper maintenance, central AC units typically last 15-20 years, furnaces 15-25 years, and heat pumps 12-15 years. Skipping annual maintenance can cut those numbers dramatically.

Yes — we handle commercial refrigeration (restaurant walk-ins, freezers, display cases), commercial HVAC, and light commercial heat pump systems. We work around your business schedule to minimize downtime.

faqs.q: Should I repair or replace my old unit?
faqs.a: Call us for an honest assessment. As a rule of thumb: if your system is over 12-15 years old and the repair costs more than half the price of a new unit, replacement usually makes more sense. We'll lay out both options with real numbers — no upsell pressure.

faqs.q: How can I lower my energy bills?
faqs.a: Annual maintenance, a programmable or smart thermostat, sealing duct leaks, replacing filters monthly during heavy-use seasons, and setting your thermostat 2-3° higher in summer / lower in winter. If your system is old and inefficient, a high-SEER replacement can cut cooling costs significantly.

tips: Check the thermostat is set to 'cool' and below room temperature
Replace a dirty air filter — this is the #1 cause of weak cooling
Make sure the outside condenser unit isn't blocked by leaves, debris, or overgrown plants
Check the breaker — a tripped breaker is common after power surges
If it's still not cooling, call us — could be low refrigerant or a failing component
Confirm the thermostat is set to 'heat' and the temperature is above the room temperature
Check that the gas valve is open (for gas furnaces)
Replace a dirty air filter
Check for a tripped breaker or blown fuse
Listen for clicking without ignition — could be a bad igniter, common but a tech needs to handle it

troubleshootingTips.issue: AC running but blowing warm air
tips: Check the thermostat fan setting — set to 'auto' not 'on'
Look for ice on the refrigerant lines — if you see it, turn the system off and call us (frozen coil from low refrigerant or airflow problem)
Replace the air filter
Don't keep running it if it's blowing warm — you can damage the compressor
Squealing usually means a belt or motor bearing issue — call us
Banging or clanking can indicate a loose part — turn it off and call
Hissing near the indoor unit can be a refrigerant leak — call us same day
Light clicking at startup is normal; constant clicking is not
Most often a clogged condensate drain line
Turn the AC off to prevent water damage
Don't try to clear it with chemicals — call us, we'll flush it properly

seasonalTips.spring: Schedule your AC tune-up before the first heat wave hits. Replace your air filter. Clear leaves and debris from around the outdoor condenser unit.
seasonalTips.summer: Set your thermostat to 78°F when home, higher when away. Use ceiling fans to feel cooler at higher set points. Close blinds during peak sun hours. Replace filters monthly during heavy use.
seasonalTips.fall: Schedule your furnace inspection before first cold night. Test your heater on a cool day so you find any problems before you actually need it. Replace the filter.
seasonalTips.winter: Set your thermostat to 68°F when home — every degree higher costs about 3% more on heating. Make sure heating vents aren't blocked by furniture. Replace filters every 1-2 months.
